This is the file to open first when reviewing the analysis. The code is shown
in the order in which the ecological analysis proceeds. The workflow itself is
run by `targets`; the code chunks below define the main targets through
`tarchetypes::tar_tangle()`.

Analytical chunks are not executed by Quarto: the first code chunk sets
`eval = FALSE` for the document, which is the method recommended by
`tarchetypes::tar_tangle()`. (`eval` cannot be repeated as a target-chunk
option because `tar_tangle()` would pass it to `tar_target()`.) After the
pipeline has been built, the clearly marked **Stored result** chunks read
already-built objects from the target store. Those display chunks override
the document setting with `eval: true`, contain no top-level assignments, and
therefore cannot accidentally become targets.

```{r}
library(targets)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(eval = FALSE)
```

# Raw data

The starting point is the TransPlant RData file, together with the reviewed
configuration tables for species names, taxonomy, functional groups, climate,
traits, and phylogeny. Importing the RData file does not alter its contents.

```{r}
#| description: Project paths and fixed analysis settings.
config <- transplant_config()
```

```{r}
#| description: Original TransPlant RData file supplied to the workflow.
#| format: file
input_rdata_file <- config$input_rdata
```

```{r}
#| description: Reviewed decisions linking local vegetation names to analysis names.
#| format: file
species_mapping_decisions_input <- file.path(
  config$root, "config", "species_mapping_decisions.csv"
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Reviewed decisions applied after TNRS name matching.
#| format: file
taxonomy_overrides_input <- file.path(
  config$root, "config", "taxonomy_overrides.csv"
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Licensed TRY trait export used by the analysis.
#| format: file
try_export_file <- config$try_file
```

```{r}
#| description: Dictionary connecting TRY variables to LDMC, LMA, and vegetative height.
#| format: file
try_dictionary_input <- file.path(config$root, "config", "try_trait_map.csv")
```

```{r}
#| description: Reviewed functional-group corrections.
#| format: file
functional_group_overrides_input <- file.path(
  config$root, "config", "functional_group_overrides.csv"
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Reviewed family and functional-group decisions for resident species.
#| format: file
resident_species_overrides_input <- file.path(
  config$root, "config", "resident_species_overrides.csv"
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Reviewed decisions used to place resident species in the phylogeny.
#| format: file
phylogeny_placement_decisions_file <- file.path(
  config$root, "config", "phylogeny_placement_decisions.csv"
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Original TransPlant objects read from the registered RData file.
current_input <- read_current_transplant_input(input_rdata_file)
```

The community table is standardised with the reviewed local species-name map
and site metadata. The next two targets then define sites and experiments from
that same community table.

```{r}
#| description: Site coordinates and regions reconstructed from the original regional table.
site_metadata <- site_metadata_from_regions(current_input$regional)
```

```{r}
#| description: Local species-name decisions read as character data for reviewable matching.
species_mapping_decisions <- readr::read_csv(
  species_mapping_decisions_input,
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character())
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Audit of every local vegetation name against the reviewed mapping decisions.
species_mapping_review <- local_species_mapping_review(
  current_input$cleanedspecies,
  species_mapping_decisions
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Final one-to-one local vegetation-name mapping used to standardise the community table.
species_mapping <- resolve_local_species_mappings(
  current_input$cleanedspecies,
  species_mapping_decisions
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Standardised plot-by-year community observations with reviewed local species names.
community <- standardize_community(
  current_input$dat,
  species_mapping,
  site_metadata
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Site table reconstructed from the standardised community data and regional metadata.
sites <- build_sites(community, current_input$regional)
```

```{r}
#| description: Experiment table defining origin, destination, treatment, duration, and inclusion.
experiments <- build_experiments(community, sites)
```

```{r}
#| description: Initial checks of site, community, and experiment identifiers and expected relationships.
community_validation <- validate_community_snapshot(
  sites,
  community,
  experiments
)
```

# Data preparation

The vegetation names are reviewed through the local mapping table and TNRS.
Only records accepted at species level enter the analysis community. The
records excluded here, together with the reason, remain available in
`vegetation_taxonomic_resolution`.

```{r}
#| description: Reviewed TNRS corrections read as character data.
taxonomy_overrides <- readr::read_csv(
  taxonomy_overrides_input,
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character())
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Distinct vegetation names submitted for taxonomic harmonisation.
vegetation_species <- sort(unique(community$species))
```

```{r}
#| description: TNRS response for all vegetation names in the community data.
community_taxonomy_response <- taxonomy_response(vegetation_species)
```

```{r}
#| description: TNRS matches combined with reviewed corrections and the registered minimum score.
community_taxonomy_review <- apply_taxonomy_review(
  community_taxonomy_response,
  taxonomy_overrides,
  config$taxonomy_min_score
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Validated vegetation taxonomy after TNRS and manual review.
community_taxonomy <- validate_taxonomy_review(
  community_taxonomy_review,
  "vegetation taxonomy"
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Explicit inclusion or exclusion decision for every reviewed vegetation name.
vegetation_taxonomic_resolution <- taxonomic_resolution_review(
  community_taxonomy
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Taxonomy table restricted to names accepted at species level.
community_taxonomy_species <- filter_species_level_taxonomy(
  vegetation_taxonomic_resolution
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Community observations restricted to vegetation names reviewed and retained at species level.
analysis_community <- filter_community_to_reviewed_taxa(
  community,
  community_taxonomy_species
)
```

TRY records are restricted to the study species, harmonised through the same
taxonomy review, screened with the registered climate and range rules, and
then summarised to species-level trait values.

```{r}
#| description: TRY variable dictionary used to select and name the three focal traits.
try_dictionary <- readr::read_csv(
  try_dictionary_input,
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Original and accepted study-species names used to restrict the TRY export.
try_filter_names <- unique(c(
  community_taxonomy_species$name_original,
  community_taxonomy_species$accepted_name_reviewed
))
```

```{r}
#| description: TRY observations restricted to study species and focal trait variables.
try_cleaned <- clean_try_export(
  try_export_file,
  try_filter_names,
  try_dictionary,
  config$error_risk_max
)
```

```{r}
#| description: TNRS response for species names occurring in the restricted TRY observations.
try_taxonomy_response <- taxonomy_response(try_side_species(try_cleaned))
```

```{r}
#| description: TRY taxonomic matches combined with the reviewed corrections.
try_taxonomy_review <- apply_taxonomy_review(
  try_taxonomy_response,
  taxonomy_overrides,
  config$taxonomy_min_score
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Validated TRY taxonomy after TNRS and manual review.
try_taxonomy <- validate_taxonomy_review(try_taxonomy_review, "TRY taxonomy")
```

```{r}
#| description: TRY observations after registered climate exclusions and range checks.
try_climate_filtered <- filter_try_climate(
  try_cleaned,
  try_taxonomy,
  config$excluded_try_climates
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Plausible-range checks for all retained LDMC, LMA, and height observations.
try_range_validation <- validate_trait_ranges(
  try_climate_filtered$observations
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Species-level LDMC, LMA, and vegetative-height summaries used in the models.
try_trait_outputs <- summarise_try_traits(
  try_climate_filtered$observations
)
```

Family and functional groups are reconstructed from the reviewed taxonomy and
the two explicit decision tables.

```{r}
#| description: Plant-family lookup for every accepted vegetation species.
taxonomy_family <- tnrs_family_lookup(
  community_taxonomy_species$accepted_name_reviewed
)
```

```{r}
#| description: General functional-group corrections read as character data.
functional_group_overrides <- readr::read_csv(
  functional_group_overrides_input,
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character())
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Resident-species family and functional-group decisions read as character data.
resident_species_overrides <- readr::read_csv(
  resident_species_overrides_input,
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = readr::cols(.default = readr::col_character())
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Family, graminoid, and woodiness assignments used in the analysis.
functional_groups <- derive_functional_groups(
  taxonomy_family,
  functional_group_overrides,
  resident_species_overrides
)
```

The CHELSA jobs remain dynamically branched because each year-variable file is
downloaded or read from cache independently. The scientific sequence—check
coordinates, retrieve monthly climate, then summarise by site and experiment—
is kept visible here.

```{r}
#| description: Checks for missing, duplicated, or reused site coordinates before climate extraction.
chelsa_coordinate_audit <- audit_chelsa_coordinates(sites, experiments)
```

```{r}
#| description: Validated site coordinates supplied to every CHELSA extraction job.
chelsa_site_coordinates <- {
  chelsa_coordinate_audit
  validate_site_coordinates(sites)
}
```

```{r}
#| description: Requested CHELSA year-variable combinations.
#| iteration: list
chelsa_job_list <- chelsa_jobs(
  config$climate_download_years,
  config$climate_variables
)
```

```{r}
#| description: One CHELSA year-variable job selected for dynamic branching.
#| pattern: map(chelsa_job_list)
#| iteration: list
chelsa_job <- chelsa_job_list
```

```{r}
#| description: Cached or downloaded monthly CHELSA values for one year-variable job.
#| pattern: map(chelsa_job)
#| format: file
chelsa_monthly_file <- run_chelsa_job(
  chelsa_job,
  chelsa_site_coordinates,
  config$chelsa_cache,
  config$chelsa_retries,
  config$chelsa_backoff_seconds
)
```

```{r}
#| description: All monthly CHELSA files combined and checked for complete site-year coverage.
chelsa_consolidated <- consolidate_chelsa(
  chelsa_monthly_file,
  sites,
  config$climate_download_years
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Annual and summer climate summaries for each study site and year.
site_year_climate <- summarise_site_climate(chelsa_consolidated$monthly)
```

```{r}
#| description: Origin, destination, and warming climate summaries for every experiment.
experiment_climate <- summarise_experiment_climate(
  site_year_climate,
  experiments
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Climate-year completeness for every experiment.
experiment_climate_coverage <- experiment_climate |>
  dplyr::select(
    experiment_id, first_year, last_year, years_expected,
    origin_years_available, destination_years_available,
    origin_missing_years, destination_missing_years,
    climate_complete, climate_summary_status, climate_coverage_note
  )
```

# Response calculation

Relative cover is integrated through time within plots. For every experiment,
horizon, and transformation, plot AUC is modelled as:

\[
\mathrm{AUC} = \mathrm{ODT} * \mathrm{species}.
\]

`ODT` distinguishes destination controls, origin controls, and warmed plots.
The warmed-minus-origin contrast is the resident response used below. The
multivariate-*t* adjustment belongs to the original within-experiment contrast
classification; it is separate from the sampling variances used in the later
meta-regressions.

```{r}
#| description: Plot-level AUC model fitted separately within experiment, horizon, and transformation.
plot_auc_formula <- auc ~ ODT * species
```

```{r}
#| description: Multiplicity adjustment used for the three planned ODT contrasts within each species.
plot_auc_contrast_adjustment <- "mvt"
```

```{r}
#| description: Significance level used to classify original winner-loser contrasts.
winner_loser_alpha <- 0.05
```

```{r}
#| description: Plot-level temporal AUC values and fixed species-pool membership for all registered horizons.
auc_inputs <- calculate_auc_inputs(
  analysis_community,
  experiments,
  config$horizons
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Within-experiment species AUC contrasts from the explicit ODT-by-species model.
auc_contrasts <- fit_auc_contrasts(
  auc_inputs$auc,
  formula = plot_auc_formula,
  contrast_adjust = plot_auc_contrast_adjustment
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Winner-loser classifications from warmed-minus-origin contrasts and fixed species pools.
winner_loser <- classify_winners_losers(
  auc_contrasts,
  auc_inputs$pools,
  alpha = winner_loser_alpha
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Completeness and consistency checks for winner-loser effects and classifications.
winner_loser_validation <- validate_winner_loser_outputs(
  winner_loser,
  auc_inputs$pools
)
```

The winner/loser results are now joined to the reviewed taxonomy, TRY traits,
functional groups, and experiment table. Climate is joined afterwards so the
descriptive data and the model-ready data remain distinguishable.

```{r}
#| description: Winner-loser observations annotated with taxonomy, traits, functional groups, and experiment metadata.
descriptive_analysis_data <- analysis_dataset(
  winner_loser,
  community_taxonomy_species,
  try_trait_outputs$summary,
  functional_groups,
  experiments
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Final analysis dataset with experiment climate and registered predictor transformations.
analysis_data <- join_experiment_climate(
  descriptive_analysis_data,
  experiment_climate
) |>
  transform_model_predictors()
```

```{r}
#| description: Reviewed five-context assignment calculated from the final experiment climate variables.
climate_context_result <- reviewed_five_climate_contexts(analysis_data)
```

This compact audit makes the main changes in data size visible without making
every filter or join a separate target.

```{r}
#| description: Row, species, and experiment counts at the principal raw-to-analysis boundaries.
analysis_data_audit <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(
    stage = "standardised community",
    record_type = "plot-year observation",
    rows = nrow(community),
    species = dplyr::n_distinct(community$species),
    experiments = dplyr::n_distinct(community$experiment_id)
  ),
  tibble::tibble(
    stage = "species-level taxonomy retained",
    record_type = "plot-year observation",
    rows = nrow(analysis_community),
    species = dplyr::n_distinct(analysis_community$species),
    experiments = dplyr::n_distinct(analysis_community$experiment_id)
  ),
  tibble::tibble(
    stage = "winner-loser data with ecological information",
    record_type = "species response",
    rows = nrow(descriptive_analysis_data),
    species = dplyr::n_distinct(descriptive_analysis_data$species),
    experiments = dplyr::n_distinct(descriptive_analysis_data$experiment_id)
  ),
  tibble::tibble(
    stage = "final analysis dataset with climate",
    record_type = "species response",
    rows = nrow(analysis_data),
    species = dplyr::n_distinct(analysis_data$species),
    experiments = dplyr::n_distinct(analysis_data$experiment_id)
  )
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    comparable_to_previous = .data$record_type == dplyr::lag(.data$record_type),
    rows_removed_since_previous = dplyr::if_else(
      .data$comparable_to_previous,
      dplyr::lag(.data$rows) - .data$rows,
      NA_integer_
    ),
    species_removed_since_previous =
      dplyr::if_else(
        .data$comparable_to_previous,
        dplyr::lag(.data$species) - .data$species,
        NA_integer_
      ),
    experiments_removed_since_previous =
      dplyr::if_else(
        .data$comparable_to_previous,
        dplyr::lag(.data$experiments) - .data$experiments,
        NA_integer_
      )
  )
```

```{r}
#| description: Missing values in ecological fields needed to understand model-specific row loss.
analysis_data_missingness <- {
  fields <- c(
    "accepted_name", "family", "graminoid_status", "woody_status",
    "LDMC", "LMA", "vegetative_height", "destination_T_JJA",
    "destination_P_JJA", "diff_T_JJA"
  )
  tibble::tibble(
    field = fields,
    missing_rows = vapply(
      analysis_data[fields], function(value) sum(is.na(value)), integer(1)
    ),
    available_rows = vapply(
      analysis_data[fields], function(value) sum(!is.na(value)), integer(1)
    ),
    total_rows = nrow(analysis_data)
  )
}
```

The six taxa below remain in the community and response calculations. They are
excluded only when defining the resident modeling cohort because they are
outside the focal vascular functional comparison or strongly determine the
early phylogenetic axes. `Juniperus communis` is the only gymnosperm in the
analyzed vegetation.

```{r}
#| description: Taxa excluded explicitly at the resident-model boundary, not during response calculation.
resident_species_exclusions <- c(
  "Gymnocarpium dryopteris",
  "Athyrium spinulosum",
  "Botrychium lunaria",
  "Equisetum arvense",
  "Selaginella selaginoides",
  "Juniperus communis"
)
```

The three inputs below deliberately read the registered CSV artifacts. This
preserves the exact numeric boundary used by the current analysis while making
that round trip visible.

```{r}
#| description: Stored winner-loser table used to construct resident effects.
resident_winner_loser_data <- read_pipeline_csv(winner_loser_file)
```

```{r}
#| description: Stored ecological analysis table used to construct resident effects.
resident_analysis_dataset <- read_pipeline_csv(analysis_data_file)
```

```{r}
#| description: Stored experiment climate-context table used to construct resident effects.
resident_climate_context_data <- read_pipeline_csv(
  climate_context_experiments_file
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Maximum-duration raw warmed-minus-origin resident effects before climate standardisation.
resident_auc_unscaled <- build_resident_auc_data_from_objects(
  resident_winner_loser_data,
  resident_analysis_dataset,
  resident_climate_context_data,
  horizons = "max",
  excluded_species = resident_species_exclusions
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Resident effects with destination temperature, precipitation, and warming standardised across experiments.
resident_scaled <- scale_resident_auc_data(resident_auc_unscaled)
```

```{r}
#| description: Final resident effect table used by climate, trait, functional, and phylogenetic models.
resident_auc_data <- resident_scaled$data |>
  dplyr::mutate(TP_z = .data$T_z * .data$P_z)
```

```{r}
#| description: Climate standardisation values used in the resident analysis.
resident_climate_scaling <- resident_scaled$scaling |>
  dplyr::filter(.data$scaled_field %in% c("T_z", "P_z", "W_z")) |>
  dplyr::mutate(
    n_distinct_experiments = dplyr::n_distinct(
      resident_auc_data$experiment_id
    )
  )
```

Sampling error is represented as independent between effect estimates. The
matrix is diagonal, in the exact effect-row order, with
`sampling variance = auc_se^2`. Experiment-clustered CR1 uncertainty is a
separate calculation for fixed-effect inference.

```{r}
#| description: Diagonal resident sampling-variance matrix with auc_se squared in exact effect order.
resident_sampling_variance_matrix <- build_sampling_variance_matrix(
  resident_auc_data,
  se_column = "auc_se"
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Checks that resident sampling variances are positive, diagonal, and exactly effect ordered.
resident_sampling_variance_check <- validate_sampling_variance_matrix(
  resident_sampling_variance_matrix,
  resident_auc_data,
  se_column = "auc_se"
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Fixed sample-size and completeness checks for the resident modeling cohort.
analysis_settings <- resident_analysis_spec(config$root)
```

```{r}
#| description: Validation of resident effects, species, experiments, and sampling-variance order.
resident_scope <- validate_resident_model_scope(
  resident_auc_data,
  resident_sampling_variance_matrix,
  analysis_settings
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Release check for the diagonal resident sampling-variance matrix.
resident_sampling_variance_validation <- resident_sampling_variance_release_check(
  resident_scope$sampling_variance_validation
)
```

# Model specifications

The response in the resident and predictor meta-regressions is maximum-duration
raw relative-cover Delta AUC: warmed minus origin. Final coefficients and
variance components are estimated with REML. ML versions are fitted only when
comparing nested climate-only and full predictor models.

All species-level models use the same random structure:

- a species random intercept;
- an independent species random slope for warming (`W_z`);
- correlated species random slopes for destination temperature (`T_z`), log
  precipitation (`P_z`), and their product (`TP_z`), using `struct = "GEN"`.

Fixed-effect uncertainty reported for final models uses CR1 clustered by
experiment, with the small-sample adjustment enabled.

```{r}
#| description: Climate-only fixed-effect formula used by resident and matched baseline models.
resident_climate_formula <- ~ T_z * P_z * W_z
```

```{r}
#| description: Species random intercept, warming slope, and correlated T-P-TP slopes used by every species model.
resident_species_random_effects <- list(
  ~ 1 | species_id,
  ~ 0 + W_z | species_id,
  ~ 0 + T_z + P_z + TP_z | species_id
)
```

```{r}
#| description: General covariance structure for the correlated T-P-TP random slopes.
model_random_covariance_structure <- "GEN"
```

```{r}
#| description: Experiment identifier used for cluster-robust fixed-effect uncertainty.
robust_cluster_column <- "experiment_id"
```

```{r}
#| description: Small-sample adjustment used for experiment-clustered CR1 inference.
robust_small_sample_adjustment <- TRUE
```

```{r}
#| description: Metafor CR1 implementation is used directly rather than clubSandwich delegation.
robust_uses_club_sandwich <- FALSE
```

## Resident climate model

```{r}
#| description: Resident climate model fitted by ML only for later nested model comparisons.
resident_climate_model_ML <- fit_meta_regression(
  data = resident_auc_data,
  sampling_variance_matrix = resident_sampling_variance_matrix,
  formula = resident_climate_formula,
  method = "ML",
  label = "resident climate ML",
  random = resident_species_random_effects,
  struct = model_random_covariance_structure,
  sparse = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Final resident climate meta-regression fitted by REML with the explicit species random structure.
resident_climate_model <- fit_meta_regression(
  data = resident_auc_data,
  sampling_variance_matrix = resident_sampling_variance_matrix,
  formula = resident_climate_formula,
  method = "REML",
  label = "resident climate REML",
  random = resident_species_random_effects,
  struct = model_random_covariance_structure,
  sparse = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Resident climate coefficients, CR1 inference, random effects, variance profiles, and fit statistics.
resident_climate_model_results <- assemble_climate_model_results(
  resident_climate_model,
  resident_climate_variance_profiles,
  cluster_column = robust_cluster_column,
  adjust = robust_small_sample_adjustment,
  club_sandwich = robust_uses_club_sandwich
)
```

## Species context classification

A species is classified only when it occurs in at least four experiments and
its observed climates identify the intercept, `T_z`, `P_z`, and `T_z:P_z`
terms. Predictions are restricted to the convex hull of climates in which that
species occurred, with warming fixed at the median across experiments. A
species is a consistent winner when its minimum fitted Delta AUC is above zero,
a consistent loser when its maximum is below zero, and context-dependent
otherwise. The class uses fitted extrema, not p-values or confidence intervals.

```{r}
#| description: Species predictions over each eligible species observed climate range and fitted-extrema classification.
species_context_bundle <- build_species_context_bundle(
  resident_climate_model,
  resident_auc_data,
  resident_climate_formula
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Counts and proportions of the three species context classes.
species_classification_summary <- summarize_context_classification(
  species_context_bundle$classification,
  "Species"
)
```

```{r}
#| eval: true
knitr::kable(tar_read(species_classification_summary))
```

## Family reconstruction and model

Family cover is reconstructed from the same retained resident species before
calculating family AUC contrasts. Squared family contrast SEs form a diagonal
sampling-variance matrix. The family model uses the same fixed climate formula
and analogous family-level random intercept and slopes.

```{r}
#| description: Stored standardised community table used to reconstruct family cover.
family_community_input <- readRDS(community_file)
```

```{r}
#| description: Stored experiment definitions used to reconstruct family cover.
family_experiments_input <- read_pipeline_csv(experiments_file)
```

```{r}
#| description: Reviewed family corrections for resident species.
family_override_table <- family_overrides(resident_species_overrides)
```

```{r}
#| description: Resident species-to-family membership using the reviewed taxonomy and explicit resident exclusions.
family_resident_membership <- build_family_resident_membership(
  resident_winner_loser_data,
  resident_analysis_dataset,
  family_override_table,
  excluded_species = resident_species_exclusions
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Reconstructed family relative cover and plot-level family AUC values.
family_plot_auc_bundle <- build_family_plot_auc(
  family_community_input,
  family_experiments_input,
  family_resident_membership
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Family warmed-minus-origin AUC effects and their direct diagonal sampling variances.
family_auc_bundle <- build_family_auc_effects(
  family_plot_auc_bundle$plot_auc,
  family_resident_membership,
  resident_auc_data
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Family climate fixed-effect formula.
family_climate_formula <- ~ T_z * P_z * W_z
```

```{r}
#| description: Family random intercept, warming slope, and correlated T-P-TP slopes.
family_random_effects <- list(
  ~ 1 | family_id,
  ~ 0 + W_z | family_id,
  ~ 0 + T_z + P_z + TP_z | family_id
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Final family climate meta-regression fitted by REML.
family_model_bundle <- fit_family_aggregated_model(
  family_auc_bundle,
  formula = family_climate_formula,
  random = family_random_effects,
  struct = model_random_covariance_structure,
  method = "REML",
  sparse = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Family fixed effects, random variation, convergence, and classification summary.
family_model_summary <- summarize_family_model(family_model_bundle)
```

The family contrast result keeps the effect rows and their sampling variances
together. The first rows and matrix dimensions can be checked after rebuilding:

```{r}
#| eval: true
knitr::kable(utils::head(tar_read(family_auc_bundle)$data))
```

```{r}
#| eval: true
print(dim(tar_read(family_auc_bundle)$sampling_variance_matrix))
```

## Trait, functional-group, and phylogenetic models

Each predictor is compared with a climate-only model fitted to exactly the same
effect rows and sampling variances. Trait models therefore have their own
matched climate-only fits because missing traits reduce their datasets. The
functional-group and phylogenetic predictors use the complete resident cohort
and share the complete-data climate-only fits.

There is no intermediate additive predictor model.

The following targets show exactly where the three model datasets come from.
Trait values are summarised once per species, log-transformed and standardised
by `prepare_trait_data()`, and then joined to the resident effects. Functional
groups use the reviewed species assignments. Phylogenetic position is obtained
from the reviewed tree, patristic distances, and the first three PCoA axes.

```{r}
#| description: Stored TRY species summaries read at the model-input boundary.
trait_summary_input <- read_pipeline_csv(try_summary_file)
```

```{r}
#| description: One reviewed LDMC, LMA, and vegetative-height value per resident species.
trait_species <- build_trait_species(
  trait_summary_input,
  resident_auc_data$species_id
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Resident effects with complete, log-scaled, and standardised LDMC.
prepared_ldmc <- prepare_trait_data(
  trait_species,
  resident_auc_data,
  resident_sampling_variance_matrix,
  "LDMC"
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Resident effects with complete, log-scaled, and standardised LMA.
prepared_lma <- prepare_trait_data(
  trait_species,
  resident_auc_data,
  resident_sampling_variance_matrix,
  "LMA"
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Resident effects with complete, log-scaled, and standardised vegetative height.
prepared_height <- prepare_trait_data(
  trait_species,
  resident_auc_data,
  resident_sampling_variance_matrix,
  "vegetative_height"
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Trait scaling values and the model-specific effect counts retained after missing traits.
trait_scaling <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  prepared_ldmc$scaling,
  prepared_lma$scaling,
  prepared_height$scaling
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Stored functional-group assignments read at the model-input boundary.
functional_groups_input <- read_pipeline_csv(functional_groups_file)
```

```{r}
#| description: Reviewed graminoid and woodiness status for every resident species.
functional_species <- build_functional_species(
  functional_groups_input,
  resident_auc_data$species_id,
  resident_species_overrides
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Resident effects joined to graminoid and woodiness status.
functional_auc_data <- prepare_functional_predictors(
  resident_auc_data,
  functional_species
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Reviewed phylogenetic placement decisions read as character data.
phylogeny_placement_decisions <- read_pipeline_csv(
  phylogeny_placement_decisions_file
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Resident-species phylogeny reconstructed from the pinned backbone and reviewed placements.
resident_phylogeny_rebuild <- build_phylogeny_from_placement_decisions(
  phylogeny_placement_decisions,
  resident_auc_data$species_id
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Exact resident-species tip order used for phylogenetic distances and PCoA.
phylogeny_species_order <- build_phylogeny_species_order(
  resident_phylogeny_rebuild$tree,
  phylogeny_placement_decisions,
  resident_auc_data$species_id
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Patristic-distance PCoA for the retained resident species in fixed tip order.
resident_pcoa_candidate <- recompute_phylogenetic_pcoa(
  resident_phylogeny_rebuild$tree,
  metadata = NULL,
  tip_order = phylogeny_species_order$species_id
)
```

```{r}
#| description: First three oriented phylogenetic PCoA coordinates for every resident species.
resident_pev_scores_oriented <- resident_pcoa_candidate$scores |>
  dplyr::select("species_id", "PEV1", "PEV2", "PEV3")
```

```{r}
#| description: PEV1-PEV3 standardised once across unique resident species.
standardized_pev_species <- standardize_unique_species_predictors(
  resident_pev_scores_oriented,
  c("PEV1", "PEV2", "PEV3")
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Resident effects joined to standardised PEV1-PEV3 coordinates.
phylogeny_auc_data <- resident_auc_data |>
  dplyr::left_join(
    standardized_pev_species$data |>
      dplyr::select("species_id", "PEV1_z", "PEV2_z", "PEV3_z"),
    by = "species_id"
  )
```

```{r}
#| description: Full continuous-trait-by-climate formula used separately for LDMC, LMA, and vegetative height.
trait_full_formula <- ~ Trait_z * T_z * P_z * W_z
```

```{r}
#| description: Full graminoid-status-by-climate formula.
graminoid_full_formula <- ~ GraminoidStatus * T_z * P_z * W_z
```

```{r}
#| description: Full woodiness-by-climate formula.
woodiness_full_formula <- ~ Woodiness * T_z * P_z * W_z
```

```{r}
#| description: Full phylogenetic-position formula with PEV main effects and their W-T-P-TP interactions.
phylogeny_full_formula <- ~ T_z * P_z * W_z +
  PEV1_z + PEV2_z + PEV3_z +
  PEV1_z:W_z + PEV2_z:W_z + PEV3_z:W_z +
  PEV1_z:T_z + PEV2_z:T_z + PEV3_z:T_z +
  PEV1_z:P_z + PEV2_z:P_z + PEV3_z:P_z +
  PEV1_z:TP_z + PEV2_z:TP_z + PEV3_z:TP_z
```

# Inference and diagnostics

## Heterogeneity

For each climate-only and full REML fit, response-scale heterogeneity is the
sum of the fitted species intercept variation, the warming-slope variation
expressed at each experiment's warming value, and the correlated T/P/T:P slope
variation expressed at each experiment's destination climate. The reported
percentage compares those components between the matched climate-only and full
fits. A negative percentage means that the fitted random component is larger
in the full model. This does not contradict a significant ML comparison: the
fixed predictor can improve the mean relationship while remaining differences
among species are re-estimated and may become larger.

```{r}
#| description: Response-scale heterogeneity components and matched climate-versus-full percentages for six predictors.
heterogeneity_bundle <- assemble_heterogeneity_synthesis(
  ldmc_model_pair,
  lma_model_pair,
  height_model_pair,
  graminoid_model_pair,
  woodiness_model_pair,
  phylogeny_model_pair
)
```

## Appendix Figure S7: model R2 and leave-gradient-out RMSE

Marginal and conditional R2 are calculated from the final REML fits, giving
each geographic gradient equal influence. Marginal R2 is the share of total
response-scale variation assigned to fixed effects. Conditional R2 includes
both fixed effects and fitted among-species variation. Sampling variance is
included in the denominator of both.

Writing the three variance parts as fixed-effect variation, among-species
variation, and sampling variation, the two reported quantities are:

\[
\mathrm{marginal\_R2} =
\frac{V_{fixed}}{V_{fixed} + V_{species} + V_{sampling}}
\]

\[
\mathrm{conditional\_R2} =
\frac{V_{fixed} + V_{species}}
{V_{fixed} + V_{species} + V_{sampling}}.
\]

For predictive evaluation, each of the 20 gradients is omitted in turn. Models
are fitted to the other 19 gradients and fixed effects predict Delta AUC in the
omitted gradient. RMSE and predictive R2 first calculate error within each
gradient and then give all gradients equal influence. Complete gradients are
resampled 5,000 times for 95% intervals.

For gradient \(g\), the squared errors are first averaged within that gradient
to obtain \(MSE_g\). With \(G\) gradients, the displayed calculations are:

\[
\mathrm{RMSE} = \sqrt{\frac{1}{G}\sum_g MSE_g}
\]

\[
\mathrm{predictive\_R2} = 1 -
\frac{G^{-1}\sum_g MSE_g}
{G^{-1}\sum_g \overline{y^2}_g -
 (G^{-1}\sum_g \bar{y}_g)^2}.
\]

Thus a large gradient and a small gradient have the same influence. The
bootstrap resamples whole gradients, never individual effect rows. The stored
columns are `marginal_R2`, `conditional_R2`, `predictive_R2`, and `RMSE`.

```{r}
#| description: Equal-gradient marginal and conditional R2 for climate-only and six full predictor models.
model_fit_r2 <- assemble_model_fit_r2(
  resident_climate_model,
  ldmc_model_pair,
  lma_model_pair,
  height_model_pair,
  graminoid_model_pair,
  woodiness_model_pair,
  phylogeny_model_pair
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Geographic gradients omitted one at a time for Appendix Figure S7.
#| iteration: vector
model_performance_gradient <- sort(
  unique(as.character(resident_auc_data$gradient_id))
)
```

```{r}
#| description: REML fits and fixed-effect predictions for one omitted geographic gradient.
#| pattern: map(model_performance_gradient)
#| iteration: list
model_performance_fold <- run_model_performance_gradient_fold(
  heldout_gradient = model_performance_gradient,
  predictor_specifications = predictor_specifications,
  full_data = resident_auc_data,
  full_sampling_variance_matrix = resident_sampling_variance_matrix,
  climate_formula = resident_climate_formula,
  random = resident_species_random_effects,
  struct = model_random_covariance_structure,
  method = "REML",
  sparse = TRUE
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Combined fold-level mean squared errors and numerical fit audits.
model_performance_cv <- combine_model_performance_folds(
  model_performance_fold
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Equal-gradient RMSE and predictive R2 with 5000 complete-gradient bootstrap intervals.
model_cross_validation_metrics <- summarise_model_cross_validation(
  model_performance_cv$fold_statistics,
  bootstrap_replicates = 5000L,
  seed = 20260914L
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Convergence, rank, partition, R2, RMSE, and predictive-R2 checks for Appendix Figure S7.
model_performance_validation <- validate_model_performance(
  model_performance_fold,
  model_performance_cv,
  model_fit_r2,
  model_cross_validation_metrics
)
```

```{r}
#| description: Release check requiring the four Appendix Figure S7 measures and their stored validation to pass.
model_performance_release_validation <- {
  model_fit_r2_file
  model_cross_validation_metrics_file
  model_performance_validation_file
  assert_model_performance_validation(model_performance_validation)
}
```

## Scientific dependency spine

This compact view follows one connected route from the original data to the
release check. Graminoid status is shown as one example of the six predictor
fits; all six formulas and fitting calls are displayed above.

```{r}
#| eval: true
tar_glimpse(
  targets_only = TRUE,
  names = c(
    "current_input", "community", "analysis_community", "auc_inputs",
    "auc_contrasts", "winner_loser", "descriptive_analysis_data",
    "analysis_data", "analysis_data_file", "resident_analysis_dataset",
    "resident_auc_unscaled", "resident_scaled", "resident_auc_data",
    "resident_climate_model", "graminoid_model_pair",
    "heterogeneity_bundle", "current_scientific_release_validation",
    "release_validation"
  ),
  shortcut = TRUE,
  degree_from = 0L,
  degree_to = 0L
)
```

## Resident models to Figure 6 and release

This focused view shows the resident climate, family, one example predictor,
heterogeneity, and Figure 6 branches. The full workflow has analogous branches
for the other five predictors and for all other figures.

```{r}
#| eval: true
tar_visnetwork(
  targets_only = TRUE,

    "family_auc_bundle", "family_model_bundle", "family_model_summary",
    "graminoid_model_pair", "heterogeneity_bundle",
    "heterogeneity_synthesis_file", "figure06_predictor_synthesis_data",
    "figure06_predictor_synthesis", "current_scientific_release_validation",
    "release_validation"
  ),
  shortcut = TRUE,
  outdated = FALSE,
  degree_from = 0L,
  degree_to = 0L
)
```

## Parts that remain less direct to audit

Four parts necessarily retain more supporting code than the central analysis:

1. TNRS harmonisation depends on an external service response plus the reviewed
   override table.
2. TRY processing depends on the licensed export and its trait dictionary.
3. CHELSA processing performs repeated file downloads and spatial extraction,
   so those jobs remain dynamically branched.
4. Phylogeny reconstruction uses pinned `V.PhyloMaker2` reference data,
   reviewed placements, branch lengths, and PCoA orientation checks.

Their inputs, audits, and final objects remain visible in the target graph, but
their low-level file and package operations stay in tested helper functions.
